prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. A fractured basalt headland: The established left basalt projection extends into teal water, its angular face split by two vertical fractures. Avoid: Projecting hard coast, no completed beach or large breaking surf yet.
2. A sheltered bend in the coast: A quiet inward curve in the bare basalt coast encloses teal water, no sediment beach at its foot. Avoid: Concave sheltered geometry, not projecting headland or already deposited sand.
3. Wind-driven waves: Three broad low teal wave crests with restrained ivory edges travel diagonally across open water. Avoid: Short surface-wave repetition; no slow tide level arrows or crashing shore contact.
4. Waves breaking on the headland: One broad teal wave breaks into ivory spray against the same fractured left basalt headland. Avoid: Contact and foam distinguish impact; keep rock face intact enough to remain recognizable.
5. Angular stones freed from the coast: Three sharp dark basalt chunks lie beside a cropped foamy water edge, freshly fractured faces visible. Avoid: Coastal context and sharp corners; no meteorite metal facets.
6. Rounded shore pebbles: Three smooth dark oval pebbles, the largest retaining a slight flat fracture face, washed by a thin teal edge. Avoid: Rounded compact stones, not tiny sand grains; no decorative polished gems.
7. A coarse pebble shore: A dense coarse band of rounded dark pebbles lies below the established headland beside teal water. Avoid: Many visible coarse stones form a shore; no smooth fine sand sheet.
8. Dark sand from volcanic rock: A small low crescent of fine dark volcanic grains with a few brighter mineral flecks, no whole coastline. Avoid: Representative sand sample with granular margin, not a soil mound or giant pebbles.
9. Sand moving along the coast: A thin dark sand ribbon curves along the teal shoreline beneath shallow wave strokes. Avoid: Transporting grains remain a narrow moving plume; no settled sheltered beach yet.
10. A dark beach in the sheltered bay: The established sheltered basalt bay now has a smooth dark sand crescent along its inner edge. Avoid: Fine continuous beach at the bay, coarse pebbles remain a different shoreline setting.
11. The rotating Earth: A dark bare-rock and teal-water Earth with irregular unfamilar land patches, one short curved rotation cue. Avoid: No modern continents, vegetation or global molten glow at this later time.
12. A shallow coastal seabed: A teal sea cross-section shallows gradually toward the familiar basalt coast, dark bottom rising gently. Avoid: Submerged geometry before tidal response; no crest standing permanently at the Moonward edge.
13. Rock hollows with raised rims: The established twin basalt hollows have clearly raised uneven rims and dry dark interiors beside the sea. Avoid: Rim height and marine setting distinguish retention geometry; no water filled before the tide.
14. The Moon’s uneven gravitational pull: Earth and a smaller pale Moon share a field; three same-direction pull arrows on Earth differ gently in length. Avoid: Schematic unequal attraction on whole Earth; no magnet or water-only upward tug.
15. A tide moving through the sea: A broad teal basin has one long shallow travelling level disturbance, with a faint alternate waterline behind. Avoid: Long basin-scale response, not a fixed double mound following the Moon.
16. The tide at this coast: At the established sloping coast, two faint waterline positions and one short vertical cue indicate a local level change. Avoid: Local depth controls the response; no permanent water mountain or numerical tide claim.

Image2 is the APPROVED COAST GEOGRAPHY reference. For any shore or pool subject keep its stepped LEFT headland and low RIGHT ridge. Any hollows/pools are the same threebasins: LARGE foreground-right pool, smaller mid-left pool and small distant middle pool, same connecting basalt rims. Waterlevel orlighting maychange; rockgeometry andcamera mustnot. Water-chemistry detailviews may use closer crops of these materials. No invented bottles, vessels, observers or biological scenery.
